Listening to talk radio/ music in that language. Watching shows helps too but I find radio really help to retain foreign languages.

I spent about 5 years without speaking english (typing and reading it a lot though), and when I flew to the states for the first time, I was back to fluent in 3 weeks, even though I couldn't understand anything that was being said to me when I got there at first, even by the flight attendants.

On the other hand, there are plenty of irregular words that I mispronounce due to lack of practice "What do you mean with the b in debt is silent?"

Learning a second language is important just to open your mind. Learning more than 2.. well I'd say that depends on what you're going to use it for.

EDIT: you can try using spaced repetition software like supermemo to maintain the language

You may feel like you lose a lot, but it comes back pretty quickly once you're back in business. If you want to maintain it at its best, read novels and watch tv series, you don't even need to do that much of it. Don't panic :)
The better you get at the language the easier it is to maintain and the less work it requires. But yes, if you don't use it it will decay. That's the same with any skill.
Spanish? Try eating at mexican restaurants or chatting up people in Spanish (store, work). It's how I keep my intermediate spanish up and add odd words.
